record.context_brief: Eigenvectors for the Tracy-Widom commuting operator
record.original_question: For the self-adjoint differential operator LTW,s acting on L^2([s,+infinity)) and defined by LTW,s := d/dx alpha_s d/dx + beta_s with alpha_s(x) = x - s and beta_s(x) = -x(x - s), study its eigenvectors.

evidence.quote: To sumarise : Question 1. Study the eigenvectors of the operator LTW,s := d/dx alpha_s d/dx + beta_s, alpha_s(x) := x - s, beta_s(x) := -x(x - s).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each real parameter $s$, consider the second-order differential operator
$$L_{TW,s} \;=\; \frac{d}{dx}\,\alpha_s(x)\,\frac{d}{dx} \;+\; \beta_s(x),$$
where
$$\alpha_s(x) \;=\; x - s, \qquad \beta_s(x) \;=\; -\,x\,(x - s),$$
acting on a suitable dense domain in the Hilbert space $L^2([s,+\infty))$ on which it is self-adjoint. Note that $\alpha_s$ vanishes at the left endpoint $x = s$, so the operator is of Sturm–Liouville type with a regular singular point at $s$.

Determine explicitly the eigenvectors of $L_{TW,s}$: describe its spectrum, find closed-form (or otherwise explicit) expressions for the eigenfunctions, and analyze their analytic properties (behavior near $x = s$, decay as $x \to +\infty$, completeness in $L^2([s,+\infty))$, and the corresponding spectral resolution).
artifact.status_search_result: The operator is of the type studied by Tracy and Widom (a second-order differential operator commuting with the Airy integral operator on $[s,\infty)$). While the existence of such a commuting pair and numerical/algebraic studies of its eigendecomposition are known, an explicit closed-form description of all eigenvectors of this specific operator appears to remain an open question; no source found verifies a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Algebras of Commuting Differential Operators for Kernels of Airy Type
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy and Widom discovered instances of commuting differential and integral operators; explicit formulas for commuting differential operators of lowest order are studied.
status_evidence.claim: The commuting differential operator associated with the Airy kernel is an active research topic without a fully explicit eigenfunction description.

status_evidence.title: On the evaluation of the eigendecomposition of the Airy integral operator
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical algorithms for computing the eigendecomposition of the Airy integral operator via its commuting differential operator.
status_evidence.claim: Eigenfunctions are computed numerically; no explicit closed form is given, suggesting the analytic problem remains open.
